data.title: Has the decline of knowledge work begun?
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对企业裁员、知识工作及教育的影响

不同观点：
• **Bukhmanizer** 认为，企业进行裁员的原因之一是它们减少了创新和改进工作，将希望寄托于AI，而不是继续进行大量小改进。他们的工作现在几乎只围绕一个概念：AI，且并没有详细的计划如何使用AI实现这些改进。

• **bryanlarsen** 提出相反观点，认为尽管AI提高了知识工作者的生产力，但并不意味着会减少对知识工作者的需求。通过历史对比，如服装制造业的部分自动化导致服装价格下降，需求增加，最终使得更多人从事该行业。因此，AI对知识工作者的需求可能反而会增加。

• **fullshark** 认为，大学学位体系需要彻底反思。当前的学位体系与实际技能需求脱节，导致学生背负沉重的债务，而学位并没有带来相应的工作保障或实际技能。

• **apercu** 对AI的实际效果持怀疑态度，指出当前的AI工具（如ChatGPT）在实际应用中经常出错，使用者需要具备相关知识才能识别和纠正这些错误。因此，虽然AI技术本身很了不起，但过度相信其能力是不可取的。

• **squigglydonut** 认为，如果希望AI产生更好的结果，必须对其提出高要求，仿佛生死攸关。

• **Glyptodon** 认为，知识工作的外包和低薪趋势早在AI普及之前就已经存在，AI只是加剧了这一趋势。AI的引入使得企业可以以更低成本获得尚可的结果，从而减少对高技能员工的需求。

• **7qW24A** 指出，过去10年中企业过度招聘，导致机构臃肿，而AI正好为企业提供了裁员的借口，即使AI并没有显著提升生产力，裁员也可能发生。

• **nopelynopington** 对AI在编写代码方面的能力持怀疑态度，认为即使最好的AI引擎也会写出糟糕的代码，且这种情况可能不会改善。但AI也可能让员工更容易应付工作，从而导致知识工作的整体质量下降。

• **iambateman** 认为，知识工作的技能分布广泛，大多数员工处于中等水平。AI的引入可能提升中等水平员工的能力，使得整体知识工作的平均能力上升。

• **carabiner** 指出，像机械工程等专业领域的知识工作受AI影响较小，因为这些领域的专业数据大多被企业锁住，公开数据较少，难以训练出高效的AI模型。

• **talkingtab** 提出一种更为宏观的社会经济观点，认为AI可能导致企业利润上升但同时减少对人力的需求，最终可能破坏整体经济。此外，企业擅长剥削技术红利，但可能缺乏创新动力。

• **alecco** 认为，像马斯克这样的企业已经通过AI找到了裁员的借口，许多企业可能也随之效仿，将大量工作外包至其他国家，这可能带来潜在的风险。

• **coolThingsFirst** 认为，当前就业市场竞争极其激烈，传统职业发展路径受阻，许多人开始转向小型创业公司或自谋出路。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI是否会真正减少对知识工作者的需求，或者反而会增加需求。
- 大学学位体系的可持续性及其与实际工作需求的脱节问题。
- AI在实际应用中的局限性及其可能带来的负面影响，如错误结果和低质量工作的增加。
- 企业裁员是否主要由AI驱动，或者只是企业借此机会进行结构调整。

data.title: Intel RealSense Stereo Depth Cameras
data.author: 1sembiyan
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Intel RealSense深度摄像头系列，包括入门级的D421模块以及其他多种型号（如D456、D457、D455f、D435、D415等），每款摄像头具有不同的视野、理想距离和功能特点，如全局快门、IMU和IP67防水防尘等级。文章还展示了这些摄像头在辅助视障人士（.lumen眼镜）、安全筛查（Thruvision）、店内运营自动化（Simbe Robotics）和工业检测自动化（ANYBotics）等领域的应用案例。此外，文章提供了SDK 2.0、文档、代码示例和教程等开发资源，并支持多种编程语言和操作系统。用户可以根据需求选择最合适的摄像头，并通过线上或授权经销商购买。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Intel RealSense及其替代产品的使用体验与技术优劣

不同观点：
• Uehreka：因Intel对RealSense产品线的不确定性（如团队裁员或停产传闻），选择了Stereolabs的ZED 2i。认为ZED 2i功能良好，但垂直安装时骨骼追踪效果不佳。同时，肯定了Stereolabs的软件更新速度。
• Symmetry：回顾了Kinect和RealSense的历史，指出Intel曾填补Kinect退出后的市场空缺，但近期关于RealSense的停产声明引发了业界恐慌，促使一些公司开发内部3D传感器系统。不过，Intel将RealSense独立出来，可能避免了彻底关闭。
• IshKebab：误以为Intel早已关闭RealSense，但发现D421模块仍是新产品，并认为其价格合理，期待更小批量销售。
• ftrobro：曾尝试RealSense但结果不可靠，推荐使用Chronoptics KEA，效果更好。
• donatj：质疑RealSense是否已停产，并讨论其硬件是否承担立体图像解码功能，或完全依赖软件处理。
• omershapira：指出这些传感器虽利润微薄但行业必需，易受企业高管成本优化影响，导致行业倒退。
• aomix：通过更换为D457型号解决了USB版本的可靠性问题，对结果满意。
• sand500：询问RealSense是否会取代Xbox Kinects。
• londons_explore：指出全球快门相机的下一代通常会使用卷帘快门以降低成本，并提高性能。
• momoschili：认为RealSense自2016年以来未有重大突破，可能被ToF或LIDAR技术取代，仅在特定工业或爱好领域有应用。
• phkahler：质疑RealSense的测距范围参数不一致，存在矛盾。
• johnmarie：推荐使用Zivid相机，认为其工业级质量和结构光技术更优，尽管价格更高。
• ycuser2：询问是否可以用RealSense拍摄180°的3D视频。

补充讨论：
• 对RealSense产品线未来发展的担忧和不确定性是讨论的焦点，尤其是关于其是否停产及独立运营的问题。
• 不同用户对RealSense的可靠性和功能性有不同评价，一些人推荐了替代产品如ZED 2i、Chronoptics KEA和Zivid。
• 技术细节如USB传输的脆弱性、快门类型、测距范围等问题也被深入讨论。
• 有对价格和硬件功能的质疑，尤其是与其他新兴技术（如ToF和LIDAR）的比较。

争议焦点：
• Intel RealSense是否已停产及其未来发展方向的不确定性。
• RealSense与其他替代产品（如ZED 2i和Chronoptics KEA）的性能和可靠性比较。
• 技术参数（如测距范围）的不一致性。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了手工制作服装的特殊价值以及对成衣质量的误解。作者讲述了自己制作被子和衣服的经历，强调了定制服装的情感联系。文章指出，所有服装本质上都是手工制作的，无论是在家中自制还是工厂生产。作者批评了人们对廉价成衣质量的偏见，尤其是对来自某些国家的服装。文章解释，成衣质量的好坏取决于品牌在材料选择、剪裁、设计和生产速度等方面的决策，而非生产地工人的技能。文章最后质疑了对东亚国家服装生产能力的刻板印象，呼吁重新思考我们对成衣质量和生产者的评价方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：服装质量、生产外包、手工与量产之间的质量差异以及通货膨胀对商品质量的影响。

不同观点：
• **量产服装质量下降与通胀关系**：alabastervlog认为，自1970年代以来，经济进步的表象实际上是商品质量下降的结果，尤其是服装。例如，现代18美元的衬衫质量远不如1940年代或1950年代的同类产品。这种质量下降导致实际通胀率被低估。

• **手工与量产的质量差异**：andrewvc指出，手工制作的皮具（如钱包）质量往往优于量产品，因为手工制作者可以选择更高质量的材料，且不追求量产的效率。然而，量产涉及的工业缝纫技术仍然需要高度熟练的工人操作，且量产设计更注重外观而非耐用性。

• **自制服装的满足感与成本**：squeedles分享了自己制作服装的经验，认为自制服装不仅能满足个人需求，还能提供创造性满足。然而，制作一件高质量衬衫需要大量时间，难以规模化生产，这也解释了量产服装为何通过降低成本来提高利润。

• **现代内衣质量下降**：fifticon提到现代男性内衣质量下降，尤其是弹性材料部分，使用寿命明显缩短，怀疑是企业为了促进重复购买而故意设计的。

• **服装生产外包的影响**：blululu强调，服装生产从发达国家外包到第三世界国家，虽然提高了企业利润，但导致了质量下降和本地工人失业。这种外包决策主要是为了降低成本，而非提升质量。

• **劳动价值与社会不公**：achenet通过自制裤子失败的经历，反思了劳动价值与社会不公问题，指出在现代经济中，编程技能比缝纫技能更有价值和回报，质疑“努力工作必有回报”的观念。

补充讨论：
• **自动化与人工参与**：tialaramex和aeneasmackenzie讨论了服装生产中的自动化程度，指出虽然部分生产环节已经完全自动化，但仍需人工参与，尤其是在质量检测和后期处理上。

• **商品质量操控与消费者困惑**：1970-1-1和rekttrader提到消费者在购买服装或食品时面临的困惑与骗局，例如在美国可以用“丝绸”宣传人造纤维，误导消费者。

争议焦点：
• **商品质量下降的原因**：一部分评论者（如alabastervlog和blululu）认为商品质量下降是企业为了追求利润而故意降低成本的结果，而另一些人（如andrewvc）则认为这是生产规模化和设计选择的结果。

• **外包与本地失业的关系**：blululu指出第三世界工人被剥削的同时，发达国家的工人也因外包而失业，认为这是一种反社会的利润追求方式，但arijun认为这种比较没有必要，因为服装质量与工人所在地无直接关系。

43450515.article_content:
All Clothing Is Handmade
2022-10-29
quilts
The idea for this quilt came to me several years ago. Besides making quilts, I make some of my own clothes and occasionally make clothes for people in my life. I made my own wedding dress and one for a college friend as well (and never doing that again).
There’s something special nowadays about something that was made or tailored just for you, whether it was done by a friend/family member or something you had made. When I was a kid, my father gave my mother a birthday gift of what was essentially a copy of her favorite dress, made by a local seamstress. The style was pretty basic, but not being sold in stores at that time. I’m sure it was quite expensive. It was very thoughtful, she loved and wore the dress for ages, until her cancer surgeries made its fit uncomfortable.
But while I love the personal connections of bespoke/self-made clothing, I want to push back a bit against some language that occurs when people (myself included) talk about store-bought clothing, especially cheaper clothing. Whether it’s the nice Lands End flannel shirt I’m wearing as I write this, or the one my husband is wearing that I made for him, or the TikTok influencer’s Shein t-shirt that rips when she tries it on… all clothing is handmade.
I made this quilt using worn textiles from friends, family, and some folks in my church and scraps from my own projects. It’s got a piece of fabric from my wedding dress and others from one of my mom’s favorite dresses. There’s a couple of my husband’s old dress shirts, bits of my father’s ties, the lining of my little sister’s worn jacket, highlights from a friend’s tunic, bits of baby dresses, another friend’s dress shirt, and more. There’s a couple little pieces of leftover fabric from that same flannel shirt my husband is wearing right now.
I pieced it ages ago, I can’t quite even remember… 2020? It’s a wonky quilt, dozens of fabrics that were never meant to sit side-by-side. A little leather just for fun and frustration. It took forever to figure out how I wanted to quilt it (large stitches with long strokes, colors matching as best I could in the blocks themselves) and then to get to it, but I’m very glad that it’s done and I can share it now.
Who Controls Clothing’s Quality
21st century textile production happens on a massive scale, one that keeps ramping up and has enormous environmental costs. The quality of mass-market textiles has dropped noticeably since the 1990s, which were also a noticeable drop from the 1970s.
When people talk about this change in quality, the language often carries a set of assumptions. These assumptions are often both geographically and racially coded. “This t-shirt was made in Honduras” or “This blouse was made in Cambodia” imply things about their quality and often subtly, sometimes not-so-subtly, attached to the people actually doing the work.
But even if one assessed ten thousand blouses made in Cambodia for their quality, any negative findings say nothing about the talents or potential of Cambodian garment workers as a whole or relate to, say, American garment workers. What they reflect instead are:
The brand’s choice of materials:
Where did the cloth come from and how was it made?
What kind of thread are they using? (Thread can make a major difference in the longevity of a garment. The recent trend of lowering thread quality to save money is why the crotch of your new pants split after a month when the last pair you got of these same pants lasted a solid 5 years.)
The cutting setup:
How many layers of fabric are being cut together?
How much time do the workers have to operate cutting tools?
How likely are things to slip and slide during the cutting process?
The actual garment design. Before a garment is made, especially in a mass-production context, decisions about construction need to be made including:
How are the seams finished?
What’s the stitch length?
How are buttons attached?
The speed at which it is being made:
Is the garment worker sewing 30 seams an hour? 60? 100?
What happens when there’s an error?
What kind of breaks does the worker get? Really?
These decisions are all made by the company that ordered the clothing and, quite possibly, also by one or more subcontractors. While brands may plead innocence and outsourcing, the cost per item they demand from their suppliers directly influences this…and they know it.
Mass-produced clothing is low quality when someone
overseeing the project
decided to make it low quality. Mass-produced clothing is high quality when someone
overseeing the project
decided to make it high quality. What country it came from and who made it is a reflection of how the company wanted to pay and treat the people making it, not of those people’s skills or potential.

data.title: The role of developer skills in agentic coding
data.author: BerislavLopac
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了生成式AI，特别是大型语言模型（LLM）对软件开发的影响。作者Birgitta Böckeler负责协调Thoughtworks在这方面的研究，并分享了她和团队的发现和思考。文章介绍了LLM在编码辅助中的主要任务类型，包括信息查找、代码生成、代码推理和转换。交互模式分为聊天界面、编辑器内联辅助和命令行界面。文章还讨论了模型属性（如训练数据、模型大小、上下文窗口）和工具的来源与托管方式（商业产品、开源工具、自建工具）。当前，开发者主要使用ChatGPT、GitHub Copilot等工具进行聊天互动和编辑器内辅助编码，未来开源世界和团队自建工具将在生成大段代码方面进行更多探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在开发中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• [ikerino] 认为AI在开发中能够提供帮助，但存在过时信息和不可预测的错误，导致开发效率下降。虽然AI能帮助完成一些项目，但产生大量无效代码，需要人工筛选和调整。
• [ferguess_k] 不支持在IDE中使用过多AI，认为基础的代码补全功能足够。强调AI可以帮助快速掌握新框架或新语言，但开发者仍需掌握核心技能，不应过度依赖AI。
• [usrbinbash] 将AI视为写作助手和高级橡皮鸭，用于讨论和解决问题，但不作为独立完成任务的代理。认为AI已经加速了工作流程，不需要更多的代理式AI。
• [myflash13] 强调AI能提升开发者的能量，使得原本只能写2小时代码的开发者能够持续工作5小时，类似使用电子辅助设备，提升效率但不会取代人类。
• [kunzhi] 认为当前的AI技术虽然不成熟，但开发者在使用AI的同时也在培训未来的替代者。尽管AI短期内不会取代人类，但未来技术发展可能会使得当前的技术显得过时。
• [mjr00] 指出很多关于AI辅助的文章没有明确说明适用范围，15k行代码的项目并不能代表大多数开发者的日常工作，认为需要更贴近实际开发场景的讨论。
• [jvanderbot] 提出AI在开发周边工具上的应用，例如开发和维护工具、日志系统等，认为这些非核心路径的任务更适合使用AI代理。
• [timdellinger] 对AI的未来持乐观态度，认为通过更好的提示和规划，AI可以更有效地编写代码，特别是在代码重用方面。
• [aschearer] 使用AI编写复杂原型，认为AI能提高生产力，但需要大量的人工指导，且随着项目规模扩大，AI的表现下降。
• [fasteddie31003] 提出通过架构抽象层（如Archigraph）来解决当前AI编码中的问题，认为这样可以更好地描述和理解应用的工作原理。
• [johnjungles] 认为AI能有效减少日常开发中的重复工作和沟通成本，特别是在处理跨工具的上下文转换时表现出色。
• [svilen_dobrev] 强调当前的LLM缺乏学习和理解能力，无法像人类一样积累经验和知识，认为AI需要进一步发展才能达到更高的应用水平。
• [jillesvangurp] 使用LLM进行日常开发，认为AI在处理TODO/FIXME、文档编写和代码转换等方面表现良好，但需要人工监督，不能盲目信任。

补充讨论：
• AI在代码重用和模块化方面的不足，导致重复代码和不一致的实现方式，是多个评论者提到的问题([adamgordonbell], [ikerino])。
• 对AI过度依赖的担忧，以及如何在使用AI的同时保持开发者自身技能的提升，是另一个值得注意的讨论点([ferguess_k], [svilen_dobrev])。
• 对未来AI技术发展的预期和潜在影响，包括对开发者角色的影响，是讨论中的一个重要主题([kunzhi], [mjr00])。

43480964.article_content:
Exploring Generative AI
Birgitta BÃ¶ckeler
generative AI
Generative AI and particularly LLMs (Large Language Models) have exploded
into the public consciousness. Like many software developers I am intrigued
by the possibilities, but unsure what exactly it will mean for our profession
in the long run. I have now taken on a role in Thoughtworks to coordinate our
work on how this technology will affect software delivery practices.
I'll be posting various memos here to describe what my colleagues and I are
learning and thinking.
Earlier Memos
▶
The toolchain (26 July 2023)
▶
The toolchain
Letâs start with the toolchain. Whenever there is a new area with still evolving patterns and technology, I try to develop a mental model of how things fit together. It helps deal with the wave of information coming at me. What types of problems are being solved in the space? What are the common types of puzzle pieces needed to solve those problems? How are things fitting together?
How to categorise the tools
The following are the dimensions of my current mental model of tools that use LLMs (Large Language Models) to support with coding.
Assisted tasks
Finding information faster, and in context
Generating code
âReasoningâ about code (Explaining code, or problems in the code)
Transforming code into something else (e.g. documentation text or diagram)
These are the types of tasks I see most commonly tackled when it comes to coding assistance, although there is a lot more if I would expand the scope to other tasks in the software delivery lifecycle.
Interaction modes
Iâve seen three main types of interaction modes:
Chat interfaces
In-line assistance, i.e. typing in a code editor
CLI
Prompt composition
The quality of the prompt obviously has a big impact on the usefulness on the tools, in combination with the suitability of the LLM used in the backend. Prompt engineering does not have to be left purely to the user though, many tools apply prompting techniques for you in a backend.
User creates the prompt from scratch
Tool composes prompt from user input and additional context (e.g. open files, a set of reusable context snippets, or additional questions to the user)
Properties of the model
What the model was trained with
Was it trained specifically with code, and coding tasks? Which languages?
When was it trained, i.e. how current is the information
Size of the model (itâs still very debated in which way this matters though, and what a âgoodâ size is for a specific task like coding)
Size of the context window supported by the model, which is basically the number of tokens it can take as the prompt
What filters have been added to the model, or the backend where it is hosted
Origin and hosting
Commercial products, with LLM APIs hosted by a the product company
Open source tools, connecting to LLM API services
Self-built tools, connecting to LLM API services
Self-built tools connecting to fine-tuned, self-hosted LLM API
Examples
Here are some common examples of tools in the space, and how they fit into this model. (The list is not an endorsement of these tools, or dismissal of other tools, itâs just supposed to help illustrate the dimensions.)
Tool
Tasks
Interaction
Prompt composition
Model
Origin / Hosting
GitHub Copilot
Code generation
In-line assistance
Composed by IDE extension
Trained with code, vulnerability filters
Commercial
GitHub Copilot Chat
All of them
Chat
Composed of user chat + open files
Trained with code
Commercial
ChatGPT
All of them
Chat
All done by user
Trained with code
Commercial
GPT Engineer
Code generation
CLI
Prompt composed based on user input
Choice of OpenAI models
Open Source, connecting to OpenAI API
âTeam AIsâ
All of them
Web UI
Prompt composed based on user input and use case
Most commonly with OpenAIâs GPT models
Maintained by a team for their use cases, connecting to OpenAI APIs
Metaâs
CodeCompose
Code generation
In-line assistance
Composed by editor extension
Model fine-tuned on internal use cases and codebases
Self-hosted
What are people using today, and whatâs next?
Today, people are most commonly using combinations of direct chat interaction (e.g. via ChatGPT or Copilot Chat) with coding assistance in the code editor (e.g. via GitHub Copilot or Tabnine). In-line assistance in the context of an editor is probably the most mature and effective way to use LLMs for coding assistance today, compared to other approaches. It supports the developer in their natural workflow with small steps. Smaller steps make it easier to follow along and review the quality more diligently, and itâs easy to just move on in the cases where it does not work.
There is a lot of experimentation going on in the open source world with tooling that provides prompt composition to generate larger pieces of code (e.g. GPT Engineer, Aider). Iâve seen similar usage of small prompt composition applications tuned by teams for their specific use cases, e.g. by combining a reusable architecture and tech stack

• [kunzhi] 认为当前的AI技术虽然不成熟，但开发者在使用AI的同时也在培训未来的替代者。尽管AI短期内不会取代人类，但未来技术发展可能会使得当前的技术显得过时。
• [mjr00] 指出很多关于AI辅助的文章没有明确说明适用范围，15k行代码的项目并不能代表大多数开发者的日常工作，认为需要更贴近实际开发场景的讨论。
• [jvanderbot] 提出AI在开发周边工具上的应用，例如开发和维护工具、日志系统等，认为这些非核心路径的任务更适合使用AI代理。
• [timdellinger] 对AI的未来持乐观态度，认为通过更好的提示和规划，AI可以更有效地编写代码，特别是在代码重用方面。
• [aschearer] 使用AI编写复杂原型，认为AI能提高生产力，但需要大量的人工指导，且随着项目规模扩大，AI的表现下降。
• [fasteddie31003] 提出通过架构抽象层（如Archigraph）来解决当前AI编码中的问题，认为这样可以更好地描述和理解应用的工作原理。
• [johnjungles] 认为AI能有效减少日常开发中的重复工作和沟通成本，特别是在处理跨工具的上下文转换时表现出色。
• [svilen_dobrev] 强调当前的LLM缺乏学习和理解能力，无法像人类一样积累经验和知识，认为AI需要进一步发展才能达到更高的应用水平。
• [jillesvangurp] 使用LLM进行日常开发，认为AI在处理TODO/FIXME、文档编写和代码转换等方面表现良好，但需要人工监督，不能盲目信任。

补充讨论：
• AI在代码重用和模块化方面的不足，导致重复代码和不一致的实现方式，是多个评论者提到的问题([adamgordonbell], [ikerino])。
• 对AI过度依赖的担忧，以及如何在使用AI的同时保持开发者自身技能的提升，是另一个值得注意的讨论点([ferguess_k], [svilen_dobrev])。
• 对未来AI技术发展的预期和潜在影响，包括对开发者角色的影响，是讨论中的一个重要主题([kunzhi], [mjr00])。

data.title: The long-awaited Friend Compound laws in California
data.author: simonebrunozzi
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于家庭和朋友共同购置和 subdividing 房产的讨论，包括法律、实际操作以及可能的社会和经济影响。

不同观点：
• **支持建立契约和社区协会**：crmd 认为需要在原始契约上建立控制机制，例如集体批准买家或拥有优先购买权，以防止家庭社区变成“普通”陌生人社区。这种情况下，有契约的业主协会是有必要的。
• **对邻里模式的兴趣**：simonebrunozzi 表示，如果邻居是朋友，会更愿意考虑在旧金山湾区购置房产，因为这种模式比传统购房更具吸引力。
• **土地成本问题**：logifail 指出，在美国某些地区购买土地非常昂贵，购买多块土地以实现家庭社区构想可能不切实际。
• **法律限制和地域差异**：njarboe 提到在科罗拉多州农村地区，法律对 subdividing 小于 35 英亩的地块有严格限制，导致无法建设小型住宅，希望能改变这种状况。
• **对市场价值的担忧**：Workaccount2 认为，虽然理论上通过建设小型住宅可以增加地块价值，但在实际中，过度细分可能导致地块贬值，需要有机制防止这种情况。

补充讨论：
• **历史对比**：cft 提到类似做法在苏联有过尝试，称为“公共公寓”，但这种模式有其历史背景和问题。
• **法律细节**：josephpmay 纠正了关于 SB 684 法案适用范围的错误信息，指出从七月起将被 SB 1123 取代，后者适用于“空置或不可居住”的单户地块。
• **设计和隐私**：diebeforei485 希望有私人开放空间，让居民共享，增加隐私性。
• **密度和城市适应性**：caycep 建议纽约风格的联排房屋可能比家庭社区提供更高的密度。boringg 则质疑这种模式是否适用于市区，并提出在郊区可能更有效。
• **经济和社会影响**：cratermoon 和 rank0 讨论了这种模式可能对短租市场（如AirBnB）的推动作用，以及是否真正缓解住房危机。dmitrygr 则担心停车问题和公共交通的现实可行性。
• **悲观看法**：ramesh31 对整体构想持悲观态度，认为这可能只是让人们背负更多债务，住在类似“胡佛村”的地方。

争议焦点：
• 这种模式是否能真正增加住房供应并缓解住房危机，还是反而会加剧短租市场问题并导致房产贬值。
• 法律和地域限制对实现这种家庭或朋友社区构想的影响。
• 设计和实际操作中的细节问题，如隐私、停车和公共交通。

data.title: Good-bye core types; Hello Go as we know and love it
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: Go 1.18引入了泛型及相关特性，如类型参数和类型约束，并提出了“核心类型”（core type）概念以简化泛型操作数的处理。核心类型旨在为泛型操作提供统一的类型基础，但在实际应用中，这种方法过于僵化。例如，对于通道操作和内置函数调用，核心类型的定义不够灵活。文章回顾了类型参数和类型约束的工作原理，并通过示例说明了如何在泛型中进行索引操作。然而，核心类型的引入也带来了问题，尤其是当类型集包含不同基础类型时，定义变得不适用。文章指出，这种方法在处理某些语言特性时不够灵活，未来需要改进以放松限制，使泛型更符合设计初衷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言的演变、特性（尤其是泛型）的引入以及对简易性的追求

不同观点：
• liampulles：赞赏Go团队对破坏性变更和规范变更的慎重态度，认为泛型是一个较大的变化且使用上存在困难，但同时也认为限制有助于避免泛型的滥用，支持团队保持语言的保守性。
• vessenes：认为Go团队在过去十年中一直在平衡特性需求和简易性，泛型是这种动态的缩影。支持保持简易性，认为这是Go相对于其他语言（如Rust）的优势，适合中级工程师团队使用。
• kubb：简单提到Go 1.25不会添加新特性，并期待未来可能加入的sum类型。
• franky47：有C++背景，将Go的泛型与C++的模板特化进行比较，表达了对更多语言支持此类特性的希望。
• Groxx：对文档中关于`close`函数的描述提出异议，提供反例并建议改进文档。同时希望增加更多灵活性扩展和高级API的安全习惯支持。
• giancarlostoro：从2011年开始关注Go，赞赏其向后兼容性，对泛型曾被强烈反对感到不满，但现在泛型加入后愿意更多使用Go。
• 762236：质疑在生成式AI可以帮助编写代码的时代，垃圾回收器是否仍然必要。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是泛型的引入及其对语言复杂性的影响。liampulles和vessenes支持限制泛型以保持简易性，而franky47则希望更多特性支持。
• 另一个讨论点是Go的简易性与特性丰富性之间的平衡，vessenes明确指出Go的目标用户群和简易性的重要性。
• 对文档改进的建议（Groxx）和向后兼容性的赞赏（giancarlostoro）也值得注意，显示出用户对文档质量和语言稳定性的关注。
• 关于垃圾回收器的讨论（762236）提出了在AI辅助编程时代对内存管理的需求变化，这是一个更广泛的技术发展背景下的思考。

43483842.article_content:
The Go Blog
Goodbye core types - Hello Go as we know and love it!
Robert Griesemer
26 March 2025
The Go 1.18 release introduced generics and with that a number of new features, including type parameters, type constraints, and new concepts such as type sets.
It also introduced the notion of a
core type
.
While the former provide concrete new functionality, a core type is an abstract construct that was introduced
for expediency and to simplify dealing with generic operands (operands whose types are type parameters).
In the Go compiler, code that in the past relied on the
underlying type
of an operand,
now instead had to call a function computing the operand’s core type.
In the language spec, in many places we just needed to replace “underlying type” with “core type”.
What’s not to like?
Quite a few things, as it turns out!
To understand how we got here, it’s useful to briefly revisit how type parameters and type constraints work.
Type parameters and type constraints
A type parameter is a placeholder for a future type argument;
it acts like a
type variable
whose value is known at compile time,
similar to how a named constant stands for a number, string, or bool whose value is known at compile time.
Like ordinary variables, type parameters have a type.
That type is described by their
type constraint
which determines
what operations are permitted on operands whose type is the respective type parameter.
Any concrete type that instantiates a type parameter must satisfy the type parameter’s constraint.
This ensures that an operand whose type is a type parameter possesses all of the respective type constraint’s properties,
no matter what concrete type is used to instantiate the type parameter.
In Go, type constraints are described through a mixture of method and type requirements which together
define a
type set
: this is the set of all the types that satisfy all the requirements. Go uses a
generalized form of interfaces for this purpose. An interface enumerates a set of methods and types,
and the type set described by such an interface consists of all the types that implement those methods
and that are included in the enumerated types.
For instance, the type set described by the interface
type Constraint interface {
~[]byte | ~string
Hash() uint64
}
consists of all the types whose representation is
[]byte
or
string
and whose method set includes the
Hash
method.
With this we can now write down the rules that govern operations on generic operands.
For instance, the
rules for index expressions
state that (among other things)
for an operand
a
of type parameter type
P
:
The index expression
a[x]
must be valid for values of all types in
P
’s type set.
The element types of all types in
P
’s type set must be identical.
(In this context, the element type of a string type is
byte
.)
These rules make it possible to index the generic variable
s
below (
playground
):
func at[bytestring Constraint](s bytestring, i int) byte {
return s[i]
}
The indexing operation
s[i]
is permitted because the type of
s
is
bytestring
, and the type constraint (type set) of
bytestring
contains
[]byte
and
string
types for which indexing with
i
is valid.
Core types
This type set-based approach is very flexible and in line with the intentions of the
original generics proposal
:
an operation involving operands of generic type should be valid if it is valid for any type permitted by the respective
type constraint.
To simplify matters with respect to the implementation, knowing that we would be able to relax rules later,
this approach was
not
chosen universally.
Instead, for instance, for
Send statements
, the spec states that
The channel expression’s
core type
must be a channel, the channel direction must permit send operations,
and the type of the value to be sent must be assignable to the channel’s element type.
These rules are based on the notion of a core type which is defined roughly as follows:
If a type is not a type parameter, its core type is just its
underlying type
.
If the type is a type parameter, the core type is the single underlying type of all the types in the type parameter’s type set.
If the type set has
different
underlying types, the core type doesn’t exist.
For instance,
interface{ ~[]int }
has a core type (
[]int
), but the
Constraint
interface above does not have a core type.
To make things more complicated, when it comes to channel operations and certain built-in calls (
append
,
copy
) the above definition
of core types is too restrictive.
The actual rules have adjustments that allow for differing channel directions and type sets containing both
[]byte
and
string
types.
There are various problems with this approach:
Because the definition of core type must lead to sound type rules for different language features,
it is overly restrictive for specific operations.
For instance, the Go 1.24 rules for
slice expressions
do rely on core types,
and as a consequence slicing an operand of type
S
constrained by
Constraint
is not permitte

data.title: Debian bookworm live images now reproducible
data.author: bertman
data.article_summary: Debian开发者Roland Clobus宣布，Debian 12.10 ("bookworm")的live镜像现已实现100%可重复构建。这一进展在Reproducible Builds邮件列表中公布，更多信息可查看Debian wiki上的相关页面。这一成就意味着用户可以验证镜像的构建过程，确保其未被篡改，提升了安全性与透明度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Debian可重现构建的相关技术和意义

不同观点：
• jcmfernandes和kragen等对这一成就表示高度赞扬，认为这是一个重要的里程碑，并向参与者表示祝贺。
• kroeckx指出，当前的可重现性仅限于从.deb文件生成.iso文件，而非从源代码生成.deb文件，后者仍在开发中。
• imcritic和amelius关注文件元数据（如时间戳）对可重现性的影响，质疑这些元数据是否被伪造或者被认为不重要。
• abdullahkhalids提出了对构建基础设施安全性的担忧，认为如果有人想在Debian包中注入恶意软件，可能会 targeting 构建基础设施，并询问是否有其他方编译这些镜像以证明构建服务器未被入侵。
• geocrasher和moondev关注可重现构建的实际应用，例如是否包含cloud-init，以及是否可以用于不可变基础设施。
• zozbot234进一步提出，这些镜像可以成为Debian基于不可变操作系统工作流的基础。
• nwellinghoff则对如何修改C代码以实现确定性编译输出感兴趣，认为这是可重现构建中的一个难点。

补充讨论：
• Cort3z作为一个新手，询问了构建过程如何可能产生非确定性输出，这引发了对时间戳等因素的讨论。
• letters90对最初声称构建可重现的消息进行了调侃，暗示对更新消息的不信任。
• curtisszmania对Linux镜像的可重现性终于实现表示兴奋，认为这是对稳定性和一致性的重大胜利。

争议焦点：
• 可重现性的实际范围：kroeckx指出当前的可重现性仅限于特定部分，而非全部构建过程。
• 文件元数据的影响：imcritic和amelius质疑文件元数据（如时间戳）对可重现性的影响。

data.title: Google’s two-year frenzy to catch up with OpenAI
data.author: totaldude87
data.article_summary: 2022年底，谷歌高管Sissie Hsiao受命在100天内打造出能与ChatGPT抗衡的产品。此时，ChatGPT已吸引逾百万人使用，甚至被视为谷歌搜索的潜在替代品，令公司感到危机。尽管谷歌拥有与ChatGPT能力相当的语言模型LaMDA，但其使用受到严格限制。面对华尔街的不安和公司内部的动荡，谷歌决定加速AI战略调整，合并DeepMind和Google Brain两大研究团队，启动代号为Bard的项目。Hsiao从各团队中挑选约100人全力推进，尽管过程中面临诸多挑战和压力，Bard项目最终取得进展。经过两年努力，Alphabet股价创下新高，投资者对其AI进展持乐观态度。这一变革被视为谷歌历史上最紧张而具文化重塑性的时期之一。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google在AI领域的表现及其与OpenAI的竞争

不同观点：
• **Google在AI领域表现出色，逐渐追赶OpenAI**：
   - [dsabanin] 认为Google的Gemini和Flash模型表现出色，尤其在深度研究和上下文窗口方面领先。Google利用其现有的产品组合和云基础设施，在整合搜索、Gmail、Google Office等服务上具有优势。此外，Google在获取训练数据方面比Apple更有优势。
   - [whyenot] 也认为Gemini非常优秀，尤其在与其其他服务（如Gmail、Docs等）的整合上表现出色。

• **Google的轻量级模型影响用户体验，导致负面印象**：
   - [Workaccount2] 指出Google在所有产品中使用轻量级模型的策略导致了用户对其AI的负面印象，尤其是在搜索结果和回答质量方面。尽管如此，Google的SOTA模型（如Gemini 2.5）表现强劲，可能已经超越OpenAI。
   - [the_clarence] 也有类似观点，认为尽管Gemini速度快且拥有较大的上下文窗口，但其答案质量较差，无法用于严肃任务。

• **Google在产品化和市场竞争中面临挑战**：
   - [janalsncm] 认为Google在transformer解码器的产品化方面表现不佳，类似于Google Meet与Zoom的竞争。OpenAI尽管不盈利且非上市公司，但在市场竞争中表现更好。
   - [tzury] 指出Google内部多个团队开发相似产品导致资源分散和焦点不集中，这是Google面临的主要问题之一。

• **Google的品牌认知和市场策略问题**：
   - [totaldude87] 认为Google面临的更大问题是普通用户将AI视为与Google搜索不同的产品，Google在用户认知战中处于劣势。即使提供更多免费服务，也难以改变这一现状。
   - [lysace] 从投资者的角度指出，Google需要一位更合适的CEO，并建议投资那些提供令人信服服务的公司。

• **对Google高层决策和历史策略的质疑**：
   - [senderista] 质疑Jeff Dean在神经网络领域的长期贡献，认为他在分布式系统研究方面更为著名。

   - [svilen_dobrev] 引用Eric Schmidt多年前的言论，质疑Google为何未能在AI助理领域取得突破，反而在其他不重要的领域（如邮箱）上浪费时间。

• Google的AI产品在整合自身服务方面具有优势，但在用户认知和市场策略上存在不足。
• 内部资源分散和高层决策被认为是Google在AI竞争中的主要障碍之一。
• 用户对Google AI产品的负面印象主要源于轻量级模型的使用和答案质量问题。

A hundred days.
That was how long Google was giving Sissie Hsiao. A hundred days to build a ChatGPT rival.
By the time Hsiao took on the project in December 2022, she had spent more than 16 years at the company. She led thousands of employees. Hsiao had seen her share of corporate crises—but nothing like the code red that had been brewing in the days since
OpenAI
, a small research lab, released its public experiment in artificial intelligence. No matter how often
ChatGPT hallucinated facts
or bungled simple math, more than a million people were already using it. Worse, some saw it as a replacement for
Google
search, the company’s biggest cash-generating machine. Google had a language model that was nearly as capable as OpenAI’s, but it had been kept on a tight leash. The public could chat with LaMDA by invitation only—and in one demo, only about dogs.
Wall Street was uneasy. More than six years earlier,
CEO Sundar Pichai
had promised to prepare for an “AI-first world” in which “an intelligent assistant” would replace “the very concept of the ‘device.’” Soon after,
eight of Google’s own researchers
had invented transformer-based architecture, the literal “T” in ChatGPT. What did Google have to show for it? Disappointing ad sales. A trail of resignations among the transformers inventors.
A product called Assistant
—the one Hsiao managed—that wasn’t used for much beyond setting a timer or playing music. All that and a half-baked chatbot for Gen Zers that gave cooking advice and history lessons. By the end of 2022, the stock price of Google’s parent company, Alphabet, was 39 percent lower than the previous year’s end.
As 2023 began, Google executives wanted constant updates for the board.
Sergey Brin
, one of Google’s yacht-sailing cofounders and controlling shareholders, dropped in to review AI strategy. Word came down to employees that the $1 trillion behemoth would have to move at closer to startup speed. That would mean taking bigger risks. Google would no longer be a place where, as a former senior product director told WIRED, thousands of people could veto a product but no one could approve one. As Hsiao’s team began the 100-day sprint, she had what she called an “idiosyncratic” demand: “Quality over speed, but fast.”
Meanwhile, another executive, James Manyika, helped orchestrate a longer-term change in strategy as part of conversations among top leadership. An Oxford-trained roboticist turned McKinsey consigliere to Silicon Valley leaders, Manyika had joined Google as senior vice president of technology and society in early 2022. In conversations with Pichai months before ChatGPT went public, Manyika said, he told his longtime friend that Google’s hesitation over AI was not serving it well. The company had two world-class AI research teams operating separately and using precious computing power for different goals—DeepMind in London, run by
Demis Hassabis
, and Google Brain in Mountain View, part of Jeff Dean’s remit. They should be partnering up, Manyika had told Pichai at the time.
In the wake of the OpenAI launch, that’s what happened. Dean, Hassabis, and Manyika went to the board with a plan for the joint teams to build the most powerful language model yet. Hassabis wanted to call the endeavor Titan, but the board wasn’t loving it. Dean’s suggestion—Gemini—won out. (One billionaire investor was so jazzed that he snapped a picture of the three executives to commemorate the occasion.)
Since then, Manyika said, “there have been a lot of what I call ‘bold and responsible’ choices” across the company. He added: “I don't know if we've always got them right.” Indeed, this race to restore Google’s status as a leader in AI would plunge the company into further crises: At one low moment, staffers were congregating in the hallways and worrying aloud about Google becoming the next Yahoo. “It's been like sprinting a marathon,” Hsiao said. But now, more than two years later, Alphabet's shares have buoyed to an all-time high, and investors are bullish about its advances in AI.
WIRED spoke with more than 50 current and former employees—including engineers, marketers, legal and safety experts, and a dozen top executives—to trace the most frenzied and culture-reshaping period in the company’s history. Many of these employees requested anonymity to speak candidly about Google’s transformation—for better or for worse. This is the story, being told with detailed recollections from several executives for the first time, of those turbulent two years and the trade-offs required along the way.
To build the
new ChatGPT rival, codenamed Bard, former employees say Hsiao plucked about 100 people from teams across Google. Managers had no choice in the matter, according to a former search employee: Bard took precedence over everything else. Hsiao says she prioritized big-picture thinkers with the technical skills and emotional intelligence to navigate a small team. Its members, based mos

data.title: Firefox Is Finally (Re)Adding Support for Web Apps
data.author: pahbloo
data.article_summary: Firefox正在为Progressive Web Apps（PWAs）添加支持，用户可以通过在Firefox Nightly版本中的`about:config`页面启用`browser.taskbarTabs.enabled`标志来体验这一功能（称为Taskbar Tabs）。目前，启用该标志尚无实际效果，但表明该功能即将推出。与其它浏览器不同，Firefox的PWA支持不会完全遵循PWA标准，而是侧重于提供更像应用程序的体验，同时保留浏览器的核心功能，如地址栏和书签。Web应用将有自己的启动图标，可以处理网站链接，并保持打开状态直到关闭。此外，任何浏览器标签都可以临时转换为“Web应用模式”，而无需重新登录。尽管该功能姗姗来迟，但其设计旨在改进当前其它浏览器的体验。

43484542.article_content:
A few months back Firefox announced it was finally adding support for Progressive Web Apps (PWAs) after years of ignoring
its own user’s requests
to do so.
If you’re running a recent Firefox Nightly build, you can now flicking the switch on an experimental hidden flag —
browser.taskbarTabs.enabled
— in the
about:config
page to enable the feature (which Mozilla is calling
Taskbar Tabs
).
Right now, enabling that flag won’t do anything (on any platform). But the fact the flag has been added ought to mean the feature itself isn’t too far behind.
In anticipation, here’s a look at what we might expect from Firefox’s overdue support for PWAs.
Firefox Web App Support is Coming
Related Story
Firefox 136 Released, This is What’s New
Firefox’s web app integration will intentionally not look, feel, or behave the same way similar features do in other web browsers, like Chromium, GNOME Web, etc.
Rather, Firefox product manager David Rubino says the aim is to
“offer features that help you get a more app-like experience for any website you choose, when you choose”
but without users feeling like they’re
not
using Firefox.
This means the browser will not focus on supporting PWAs
specifically
, i.e., all of the features and capabilities found in the
PWA spec
and supported in other browsers/platforms (like Android).
Similarly, Rubino says web apps in Firefox will
not
use a minimal browser frame and will continue to show a main toolbar with address bar, extensions, bookmarks – though the ‘new tab’ button will be replaced with a button to open a normal Firefox window.
“Web apps are still websites in a web browser, so the goal will be to fully maintain access to features that help you with the website itself, while de-emphasising features that are about managing multiple websites,”
he adds.
Visual finesse aside, Firefox’s upcoming
Taskbar Apps
feature will do most of what you’d expect:
Web apps show their own launcher icons in app menus/docks/taskbars
Web apps should remain open until closed
Web apps can handle links to their website instead of opening a browser window/tab
It will also do a few things differently, too.
The plan it to allow any browser tab to transition to ‘web app mode’, even temporarily, without the need to sign-in again. Web apps will support link association, e.g., clicking an X link in a normal Firefox window open the X web app (if installed) – the way things work on mobile.
“I think we can improve upon the current experience offered by other web browsers by offering one-step setup, retaining access to core browser features, and allowing links to be “captured” automatically,”
Rubino concludes.
Considering how long web app tools, single-site browsers and PWA integrations have been knocking around, Firefox’s proposed approach reads more like ‘minimum-viable product with minimum of effort’ than an innovative spin on the concept.
However, better late than never.
Enable Web Apps in Firefox Nightly
Vertical tabs, proper profile management, and tab groups are three long-standing user requested features Firefox has finally gotten around to adding (latter two still in beta).
Now, support for “installing” web apps joins them.
When introducing its proposal, Mozilla devs said they’d listen to feedback from users about it but then went quiet, not providing any updates or responses to questions raised.
The latest Firefox nightly builds on Windows, macOS and Linux gain a hidden preference to enable the new ‘taskbar tabs’ (aka web apps) feature so work on the feature has clearly continued despite a lack of public engagement on it.
Alas, flipping the preference to
true
doesn’t appear to enable/activate anything yet, on Windows, macOS or Linux.
But if the feature is something you’d use, and you keep a copy of Firefox Nightly installed, it will be worth keeping an eye on things in the next few weeks…

data.title: An Interview with Zen Chief Architect Mike Clark
data.author: Smaug123
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是Casey Muratori对Zen架构首席设计师Mike Clark的采访总结。Zen架构是x86生态系统中极为重要的微架构，帮助AMD在CPU市场份额上从10%提升至25%。采访中，Mike Clark讨论了x64指令集架构（ISA）在低功耗设计中的表现，指出x64和ARM在功耗和性能上并无根本差异，主要是市场需求不同导致优化方向不同。对于x64的4k页大小限制问题，Clark表示更大页尺寸有助于提高TLB效率，但4k到2mb的直接跳跃过大，可能需要中间尺寸。整体而言，Clark强调微架构中的各种差异更多是设计上的取舍，而非根本性问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术采访的内容和相关技术细节的准确性

不同观点：
• [whizzter] 认为采访内容虽然有趣但有些脱离实际。他指出，采访讨论了向量、较长的基本块和缓存利用等问题，但现实世界中的代码（如JS）往往不使用这些技术。他认为苹果通过垂直整合在这方面做得更好，并建议将晶体管资源用于优化处理分支代码的结构（如更大的UOP缓冲区、BTB缓冲区和缓存）。

• [adgjlsfhk1] 对采访表示高度赞赏，认为这类技术性采访非常有价值，并希望看到更多类似的内容。

• [IshKebab] 对采访中的一个具体论点提出质疑，即x86指令密度是否优于ARM。他引用了一个外部资源（链接）来支持ARM的指令密度通常优于x86的观点。此外，他还对x86和ARM在存储顺序上的权衡提出了不同看法，认为软件无论如何都需要同步，因此某些论点不成立。

补充讨论：
• [levodelellis] 对采访表示赞赏，并提出了两个具体的技术问题：1) 什么因素影响分支预测器？2) 为什么没有条件异常来替代某些条件检查？

争议焦点：
• 采访内容是否过于理想化，脱离实际应用（[whizzter]的观点），还是更倾向于理论且技术性强（[adgjlsfhk1]和[IshKebab]的正面评价）？

Zen is one of the most important microarchitectures in the history of the x86 ecosystem. Not only is it the reigning champion in many x64 benchmarks, but it is also the architecture that enabled AMD’s dramatic rise in CPU marketshare over the past eight years: from 10% when the first Zen processor was launched, to 25% at the introduction of Zen 5.
I recently had the honor of interviewing none other than Zen’s chief architect, Mike Clark. I only had 30 minutes, but I tried to fit in as many of our microarchitecture questions as I could! Subscribers to
Computer Enhance
will recognize many of them as ones we’ve collectively wondered about during Q&A’s in the
Performance-Aware Programming series
- and I’m delighted to report that, as you’ll see, Mike gave detailed answers to all of them.
Below is the edited transcript of our conversation. I’ve tried to keep it as accurate as possible to the original audio, while reworking the phrasing to be appropriate for reading rather than listening. I have also had AMD approve the transcript to ensure accuracy, and I will be working with them to release an extended video version as well.
Now, without further ado, my interview with Mike Clark:
CASEY:
You will often hear “people on the internet” say that ARM as an ISA is better for low power than x64. People like me who study ISAs tend to be skeptical of this claim. As a hardware designer, are there any specific things about the x64 ISA that you find difficult to deal with for low-power designs?
MIKE:
Having spent my career working on x86, I might have a bias here! I do think each ISA has its own quirks that influence some of the microarchitecture. But at the base level, we can build low-power x86 designs as well as ARM can, and ARM can build high frequency, high performance designs as well as x86 can. None of the quirks are really limiting you on the microarchitecture. The reality is that the markets we've been targeting have been different, so they've driven the architectures to optimize for different design points. ARM is in much lower power markets where x86 hasn't had the market share to chase.
On the x86 side, the higher performance / higher frequency devices are the established market that our devices have to compete in, so that's where our design focus is. We could build the same Zen microarchitecture with an ARM ISA on top instead. We could deliver the same performance per watt. We don't view the ISA as a fundamental input to the design as far as power or performance.
CASEY:
So the memory model, whether the instructions are variable length, those sorts of things don’t factor in? None of the differences are big enough to matter?
MIKE:
No. It may take a little bit more microarchitectural work for us to account for stronger memory order on the x86 side, but of course the software has to account for the weaker memory ordering on the ARM side. So there are tradeoffs.
Variable length instructions are harder than fixed length, but we've created techniques like the uop cache, and it also gives us better density overall by having smaller instructions. x86 can put more work into each instruction byte, so we can have denser binaries and increase performance that way.
So these are all just tradeoffs in the microarchitecture. They’re not fundamental issues for delivering performance per watt at the end of the day.
CASEY
: Similar question, but moving to the OS side of things: does the 4k page size on x64 create problems for you architecturally by limiting the L1 cache size due to how tagging works? Would architectures like Zen benefit if x64 operating systems moved to 2mb pages as the smallest page size, or perhaps a 16k or 64k page size if you were to introduce that in a future architecture?
MIKE
: Definitely. We always encourage developers to use larger page sizes if they can, because it gives us a lot more capacity in our TLBs and therefore less TLB pressure overall. But we have the ability to combine 4k pages into larger pages in our TLB if the OS allocates them sequentially. We can turn four 4k pages into a 16k page if they are virtually and physically sequential. That's been a technique we've used even since the original Zen to help software get the benefits of larger page sizes without moving away from 4k pages.
However, 4k to 2mb is a big jump. We're always looking for ways to allow our software partners to have larger page sizes, but maybe something in between is more appropriate.
CASEY
: Just to poke a little further at that, for the L1 cache specifically, you're hitting up against the limit of the address bits. Have you ever wanted to put in bigger L1 caches, but found that you couldn't becaus

data.title: Linux kernel 6.14 is a big leap forward in performance and Windows compatibility
data.author: CrankyBear
data.article_summary: Linux kernel 6.14, released in March 2025, brings significant performance improvements and enhanced Windows compatibility, making it a major update for both gamers and general users. Key features include the NTSYNC driver, which boosts performance of Windows applications and games on Linux via Wine and Steam Play. It also adds support for AMD RDNA 4 graphics cards and the RADV driver, enhancing gaming graphics performance. For AI workloads, the kernel introduces the AMDXDNA driver for AMD's neural processing units. Other enhancements include better power management for AMD and Intel processors, Rust language integration, support for Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite, and fixes for vulnerabilities like GhostWrite. Overall, this release marks a substantial advancement in Linux's capabilities across multiple domains.

• TheCleric对未按计划发布版本表示自责，纯粹是因为个人失误而忘记按时发布，并对此表示懊悔。
• andy_xor_andrew对新增的低级原语（特别是为模拟不同内核行为而存在的原语）被加入Linux内核的过程表示好奇，并提到可能是由于Steam Deck和Proton的流行推动了这一变化。
• cadamsdotcom通过引用数据指出Wine将获得巨大收益，并提到未来可能出现的GPIO重大变化。
• diggan引用了Linus的短日志，表明上周相对平静，并质疑发布说明中对某些功能的夸大描述。

• jmclnx对模拟Windows原语的功能表示不满，认为这是受微软影响的结果，并希望BSD能保持独立性。

• 争议的焦点在于新增的低级原语是否必要，尤其是为了模拟不同内核行为以支持游戏功能。

43483567.article_content:
Business
Home
Business

Linux kernel 6.14 is a big leap forward in performance and Windows compatibility
The new release is finally here with cutting-edge features that should please gamers.
Written by
Steven Vaughan-Nichols,
Senior Contributing Editor
March 26, 2025 at 4:19 a.m. PT
Mike Hill/Getty Images
It's nice to know I'm not the only one who can blow a deadline. Linux Torvalds confessed that he'd love to have had "
some good excuse for why I didn't do the 6.14 release yesterday
on my regular Sunday afternoon release schedule. …  But no. It's just pure incompetence. Because absolutely nothing last-minute happened yesterday, and I was just clearing up some unrelated things in order to be ready for the merge window. And in the process just entirely forgot to actually ever cut the release. D'oh."
Also:
How to compile your first Linux kernel (and 3 reasons why you should)
Despite the minor delay, Linux 6.14 arrives packed with cutting-edge features and improvements to power upcoming Linux distributions, such as the forthcoming
Ubuntu 25.04
and
Fedora 42
.
The big news for desktop users is the improved
NTSYNC
driver, especially those who like to
play Windows games or run Windows programs on Linux
. This driver is designed to emulate Windows NT synchronization primitives. What that feature means for you and me is that it will significantly improve the performance of Windows programs running on
Wine
and
Steam Play
.
Also:
EU OS takes a 'layered' approach to its new Linux distro for the public sector
Linux gamers are eagerly awaiting this release. YouTube Linux video host Gardiner Bryant proclaimed, "
NTSYNC will change Linux gaming forever.
" On Reddit, one poster said, "
NTsync hits all points
. It's fast, portable, robust, and correct. The correctness comes from just straight up implementing Windows style synchronization semantics in a kernel module rather than trying to jury-rig or iterate on the futex/futex2 interface."
Gamers always want the best possible graphics performance, so they'll also be happy to see that Linux now supports recently launched
AMD RDNA 4
graphics cards. This approach includes support for the AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT and RX 9070 graphics cards. Combine this support with the
recently improved open-source RADV driver
and AMD gamers should see the best speed yet on their gaming rigs.
Of course, the release is not just for gamers. Linux 6.14 also includes several AMD and Intel processor enhancements. These boosts focus on power management, thermal control, and compute performance optimizations. These updates are expected to improve overall system efficiency and performance.
This release also comes with the
AMDXDNA driver
, which provides official support for AMD's neural processing units based on the XDNA architecture. This integration enables efficient execution of
AI workloads
, such as convolutional neural networks and large language models, directly on supported AMD hardware.
Also:
Finally, a Linux laptop with a brilliant display and performance that rivals my MacBook
While
Rust has faced some difficulties in recent months in Linux
, more Rust programming language abstractions have been integrated into the kernel, laying the groundwork for future drivers written in Rust. As Greg Kroah-Hartman, the stable Linux kernel maintainer, recently pointed out, with "rust misc driver bindings and other rust changes to make misc drivers actually possible. I think
this is the tipping point
, expect to see way more rust drivers going forward now that these bindings are present."
Besides drivers, Miguel Ojeda,
Rust for Linux
's lead developer, said recently that the introduction of the macro for smart pointers with Rust 1.84: derive(CoercePointee) is an "
important milestone on the way to building a kernel that only uses stable Rust
functions." This approach will also make integrating C and Rust code easier. We're getting much closer to Rust being grafted into Linux's tree.
In addition, Linux 6.14 supports Qualcomm's latest
Snapdragon 8 Elite mobile processor
, enhancing performance and stability for devices powered by this chipset. That support means you can expect to see
much faster Android-based smartphones
later this year.
Also:
The 4 most Windows-like Linux distros to try because change is hard
This release includes a patch for the so-called
GhostWrite vulnerability
, which can be used to root some
RISC-V processors
. This fix will block such attacks.
Additionally, Linux 6.14 includes improvements for the copy-on-write
Btrfs file system/logical volume manager
. These primarily read-balancing methods offer flexibility for different RAID hardware configurations and workloads. Additionally, support for uncached buffered I/O optimizes memory usage on systems with fast storage devices.
In short, the Linux kernel 6.14 represents a major step forward in Linux's evolution, offering a robust set of features that cater to diverse user needs, from gaming enthusiasts to AI researchers and

data.author: tanelpoder
data.article_summary: GhidraMCP 是一个允许大型语言模型（LLM）自动逆向工程应用程序的 Model Context Protocol（MCP）服务器。它利用 Ghidra 的核心功能，为 MCP 客户端提供多种工具，包括反编译和分析二进制文件、自动重命名方法和数据、列出方法、类、导入和导出等功能。安装步骤包括下载 GhidraMCP 插件和 Python MCP 客户端，然后在 Ghidra 中安装扩展。用户可以通过编辑配置文件将 Claude Desktop 或 5ire 等 MCP 客户端与 GhidraMCP 集成。该项目使用 Apache-2.0 许可证，主要使用 Java 和 Python 编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过LLM（大型语言模型）和MCP（Machine Code Processing）工具将专有二进制文件转换为源代码的潜力和挑战。

不同观点：
• randomtoast希望未来有一个工具可以一键将专有二进制文件转换为源代码，提到现有的开源项目（如OpenGothic和openage）需要多年社区努力。
• xX_crazy420_xX认为LLM需要以抽象语法树（AST）为核心，因为代码是树状结构而非线性，当前模型缺乏对层次结构的有效推理能力。
• qwertox询问当前哪些工具可以调用MCP，并希望在ChatGPT、Claude和Gemini的网页界面中指定MCP端点和功能，以便远程调用服务器。
• mdaniel分享了有关Ghidra和LLM整合的视频链接，并提到Malimite（iOS和macOS反编译器）的讨论。
• sorenjan推荐了一个YouTube频道，并提到其技术内容和复古OS图形编辑的趣味性。
• npace12分享了radare2的MCP工具链接。
• brokensegue分享了将Ghidra内容粘贴到LLM中并要求其解析的失败经验，希望有此类基准测试。
• celesian希望MCP服务器有更多功能，如对程序的任意读写，举例自我解压CTF挑战。
• enigma101以隐喻方式表示这打开了“潘多拉的盒子”。
• ngneer提出思考实验，如果所有二进制文件都能被完美逆向工程，将如何改变安全领域。
• Everdred2dx询问是否有人正在制作MCP服务器的“目录”，认为在GitHub上搜索不够便捷。
• dang分享了相关视频链接，内容为GhidraMCP如何利用AI反向恶意软件。
• userbinator认为逆向工程需要精确和仔细推理，LLM的统计推断难以胜任此工作。
• securemepro认为这是重大变革，期待在darkcrew ai项目中应用。
• dprophecyguy表达了对作者lauriewired的喜爱。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到具体工具和项目，如Ghidra、radare2、MCP服务器及其应用场景。
• 争议焦点在于LLM在逆向工程中的有效性和潜力，部分人认为LLM缺乏层次推理能力，难以取代人工。
• 讨论还涉及对未来技术发展的期望和安全影响的思考。

ghidraMCP
ghidraMCP is an Model Context Protocol server for allowing LLMs to autonomously reverse engineer applications. It exposes numerous tools from core Ghidra functionality to MCP clients.
ghidraMCP_demo.mp4
Features
MCP Server + Ghidra Plugin
Decompile and analyze binaries in Ghidra
Automatically rename methods and data
List methods, classes, imports, and exports
Installation
Prerequisites
Mac / Windows
Install
Ghidra
Python3
Ghidra
First, download the latest
release
from this repository. This contains the Ghidra plugin and Python MCP client. Then, you can directly import the plugin into Ghidra.
Run Ghidra
Select
File
->
Install Extensions
Click the
+
button
Select the
GhidraMCP-1-0.zip
(or your chosen version) from the downloaded release
Restart Ghidra
Make sure the GhidraMCPPlugin is enabled in
File
->
Configure
->
Developer
Video Installation Guide:
ghidra_MCP_Install.mp4
MCP Clients
Theoretically, any MCP client should work with ghidraMCP.  Two examples are given below.
Example 1: Claude Desktop
To set up Claude Desktop as a Ghidra MCP client, go to
Claude
->
Settings
->
Developer
->
Edit Config
->
claude_desktop_config.json
and add the following:
{
"mcpServers"
: {
"ghidra"
: {
"command"
:
"
python
"
,
"args"
: [
"
/ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO/bridge_mcp_ghidra.py
"
]
}
}
}
Alternatively, edit this file directly:
/Users/YOUR_USER/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
Example 2: 5ire
Another MCP client that supports multiple models on the backend is
5ire
. To set up GhidraMCP, open 5ire and go to
Tools
->
New
and set the following configurations:
Tool Key: ghidra
Name: GhidraMCP
Command:
python /ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO/bridge_mcp_ghidra.py
Building from Source
Build with Maven by running:
mvn clean package assembly:single
The generated zip file includes the built Ghidra plugin and its resources. These files are required for Ghidra to recognize the new extension.
lib/GhidraMCP.jar
extensions.properties
Module.manifest

data.title: Kilo Code: Speedrunning open source coding AI
data.author: ofou
data.article_summary: Kilo Code 是一个由 JP Posma 领导的快速发展的开源 AI 编程代理项目，旨在实现“人人编程”的梦想，让所有人都能轻松塑造数字世界。受先前火山灰中复原古图书馆项目的成功启发，团队强调极速推进和社区协作。团队在两周内迅速组建并发布了初期版本，改进了多个功能，如无需创建外部账户、支持多种模型、优化用户体验等。他们计划通过快速迭代，从简单项目入手，逐步支持更复杂的编程任务。Kilo Code 的目标是构建最用户友好的 AI 编程代理，并通过开放源代码与社区分享最佳实践，以推动整个 AI 编码领域的发展。团队正在积极招聘，并提供免费使用额度以吸引用户反馈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码代理的未来发展及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **乐观支持**：adamgordonbell 引用JP的观点，认为小型团队可以通过快速行动、贴近用户需求，在AI编码代理领域取得领先，最终成为赢家。JP对项目充满信心，认为现有的LLM（大语言模型）已经非常强大，尽管有些粗糙和不完善的地方，但这些问题会逐渐解决，关键在于谁能最快解决这些问题。

• **完全自动化设想**：realharo 提出一种设想，认为如果AI能够为数十亿的程序员、艺术家、科学家提供服务，那么人类是否还有必要参与其中，AI是否可以自主运行并生成比人类更好的创意。

• **工具比较与技术优势**：xnx 认为Gemini 2.5目前在AI编码方面处于领先地位，尤其是其大上下文窗口和惊人的单次示例。jiri 则直接比较该项目与roo code和GitHub Copilot的区别，cpldcpu 也质疑该项目是否能建立差异化产品，因为代码代理领域已经非常拥挤。

• **项目愿景与用户激励**：janpaul123（JP本人）回应社区问题，列举了一系列项目改进想法和功能计划，邀请用户反馈他们最希望实现的功能。bluelightning2k 则批评项目类似于通过小额免费资金吸引用户以展示给风投，而不是提供真正的独特价值。

• **商业模式质疑**：quikoa 对项目的盈利模式提出质疑，想知道如果不对用户或LLM供应商收费，项目如何维持运营。

• **开放性与真实性争论**：rounce 质疑该项目是否是真的开源项目，还是只是通过“部分开放”来吸引用户进入付费体系。

• **GenAI的实际应用与局限**：tristor 认为现有的GenAI工具还不能取代人类工程师编写代码，他更希望AI能帮助测试和文档化软件，而不是直接参与编码工作。yapyap 则用“编程对所有人”的比喻，指出AI代理只是降低了编程门槛，类似于Google翻译对语言学习的帮助。

补充讨论：
• **对快速行动的评价**：suddenlybananas 认为“快速行动的社区能取得惊人成就”这一观察显得陈词滥调，而handfuloflight 对“快速改进软件而不是建立漂亮网站”的说法表示调侃。

争议焦点：
• 该AI项目是否能真正建立差异化并取得成功，尤其是在竞争激烈的代码代理领域。
• 项目的开放性与商业模式是否透明，是否只是为了吸引用户和风投资金。
• GenAI是否能真正替代人类工程师，还是更适合作为辅助工具来提高生产力。

Last year, the project that I led (
Vesuvius Challenge
) achieved a
breakthrough in resurrecting an ancient library from the ashes of a volcano
(and they’re
still going
). This success taught me an important lesson:
an extremely fast-moving community can achieve incredible things.
This seems obvious, but few do it! Since then I’ve been thinking about how to apply this lesson to other spaces, such as helping my friend Steve at
Val Town
prototype an
AI agent
.
Since then I’ve been thinking a lot about AI agents. They’re the closest I’ve seen to the dream of “programming for all”: all humans shaping our digital worlds
(“moldable as clay”)
. This is something that has
long
interested
me, and I think its time has come. Gone are the days of thinking of code directly—AI agents will produce code “by the kilo”. Enter:
Kilo Code
.
There are already a million AI agent companies out there, so why another one? Me and my team are an
impatient bunch
, and we want to quickly apply this idea of an extremely fast-moving community to AI agents. We’ve been living this extreme focus on speed already:
Two weeks ago, I dropped everything in my life to build the first version.
A week later we had assembled a team of 10 (full time).
We then forked the
Roo Code
VSCode extension (which itself is a fork of
Cline
).
Since then, we shipped a bunch of small improvements (more about that below).
By Friday, we’ll have fixed two of
your requests
.
Next week, we’ll do ~10 more improvements.
Most importantly, we want to build this with you. We would love your continuous feedback (on Github and Discord), and we have a free tier (with $15 in free tokens a month!) in order to thank you—and for the best feedback we’ll give out more free tokens. The goal is to create the most user-friendly AI coding agent, as quickly as possible.
Meet the team
The team came together within a week, which means that we’ve self-selected for folks who value speed, and are down for adventure. Here are a few of us:
I’m leading the team (
JP Posma
).
Justin Halsall
leads developer relations. He has worked on an
AI company
for the last 5 years, is the open source maintainer of
rrweb
, and an Apache contributor.
Johan Otten
is our lead developer. After building products for teaching kids to code, he’s now excited to better teach LLMs to code.
In addition, we’re well-funded, and hiring. (If you’re interested mail us at
hi@kilocode.ai
. We’re remote-first, but with offices in SF and Amsterdam. Expect to work really hard and have a ton of fun.)
Small fixes shipped
We’re serious about speed! In a few days we’ve plucked some low-hanging fruit:
No need to create an OpenRouter account (use our own proxy)
No need to pay and use a credit card (batteries included free tier using Claude 3.7 Sonnet)
No need to select a model (good defaults)
No need for telemetry acceptance (we send what we need to improve the product and are transparent about what we send and how we use it)
No need to set auto acceptance (vibe coding—but you can turn it off)
Support for DeepSeek in Fireworks (super fast)
Multiple onboarding improvements (after doing user testing)
Next week we’ll similarly focus on low-hanging fruit. Tell us what you want to see, and we’ll give out more free tokens for the best ideas!
Secret Master Plan
Besides quickly building with the community, we do need some rough direction of where to take things. We started with an AI agent (as opposed to a Copilot/Cursor-style UI), because we want to build the future we want to see, and which we think is coming. We want to build for the dream of billions of programmers; billions of artists; billions of scientists—using computing as moldable clay.
However, right now AI agents only work well for smaller projects, and for novice/non-programmers. But we think we can quickly make them better, and move upmarket to more advanced use cases (Clay Christensen “
Innovator’s Dilemma
”-style).
For this, we’ll be part of the larger community of AI coding companies. Hopefully we can bring meaningful new ideas to the space, as well as quickly implement the best ideas that we see from others. Since our extension is open source, we encourage everyone (e.g. our upstream Cline and Roo Code) to use our best code and ideas.
We have some ideas already, many of which are already being pioneered by other tools, and some which are more out there:
Instant app
- Type an idea, press Enter (or Google-style “I’m feeling lucky!”), get a live app with a backend and database.
Up-to-date docs -
Crawl docs automatically, so whenever you need to find the latest version of your favorite tool, everything is up to date.
Prompt/product-first workflows
- Not even looking at any code; i

data.title: 'Naive' science fan faces jail for plutonium import
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 24岁的伊曼纽尔·利登（Emmanuel Lidden）因违反核不扩散法，向其父母位于悉尼的住所邮寄钚样本，面临可能的10年监禁。他出于对化学元素的热爱，试图收集所有元素，但在从美国网站购买并邮寄到澳大利亚后，引发了危险品事故。尽管其律师辩称他并无恶意，只是“无辜的收藏者”和“科学迷”，检方则认为其行为助长了非法市场的需求。利登因此失去火车司机工作，目前在快餐店打工，案件将于4月11日宣判。

  - perihelions怀疑是否存在混淆，认为可能是将钚与其他元素（如钋）混淆了。

• **关注雇主和个人行为的责任**：

  - puppycodes指出小剂量的铀常用于测试盖革计数器，且钚的不同同位素在危险性上差异很大。

  - palmotea质疑是否私人拥有钚在美国是合法的，或者该销售网站是否即将被关闭。
  - mmooss询问Lidden持有的钚的数量和浓缩程度。

43449645.article_content:
Read full article
Maeve Bannister
21 March 2025 at 12:30 am
·
3-min read
Link copied
A "science nerd" who wanted to collect all the elements of the periodic table could face jail time after ordering radioactive material over the internet.
But Emmanuel Lidden, 24, will have to wait to learn his sentence after breaching nuclear non-proliferation laws by shipping samples of plutonium to his parents' suburban Sydney unit.
The incident sparked a major hazmat incident, with Australian Border Force (ABF) officials, firefighters, police and paramedics all attending the scene in August 2023.
The "innocent collector" wanted all the elements of the periodic table, his lawyer said. (Alan Porritt/AAP PHOTOS)
Far from any intent to build something nefarious like a nuclear weapon with the material, Lidden's lawyer John Sutton described his client as an "innocent collector" and "science nerd" who had been left flipping burgers after being sacked from his job following the incident.
ADVERTISEMENT
"He did not import or possess these items with any sinister intent ... these were offences committed out of pure naivety," Mr Sutton told Sydney's Downing Centre District Court on Friday.
"It was a manifestation of self-soothing retreating into collection, it could have been anything but in this case he latched onto the collection of the periodic table."
Lidden had also been a keen collector of stamps, bank notes and coins.
But prosecutors said describing the young man as a simple collector and science nerd were a mischaracterisation.
This sort of incident where "collectors" sought illegal material created a market that might not have otherwise existed, the court was told.
Mr Sutton argued border force officials had engaged in duplicitous and unfair conduct by returning some of the material to Lidden after initially seizing it.
ADVERTISEMENT
"(Lidden) knew this was a radioactive substance but he was allowed to possess it, and perhaps he thought it was because it was a minimal quantity," Mr Sutton said.
"There was no Sherlock Holmes detection here by the ABF, the packages had (Lidden's) address and his name ... investigators were aware he had obtained this material and it was in a very small quantity."
The seizure in a hazmat incident was a massive overreaction, the defence lawyer said. (Bianca De Marchi/AAP PHOTOS)
Lidden ordered the items from a US-based science website and they were delivered to his parents' home.
The seizure of the items in the hazmat incident was described as a "circus" by Mr Sutton.
"The level of the response was a massive overreaction given what the investigative authority already knew," he added.
"Rather than give (Lidden) an opportunity to return the items, the kitchen sink was thrown at him, along with the utensils inside."
ADVERTISEMENT
Formerly a trainee train driver, Lidden lost his job with Sydney Trains after disclosing to his employer that he was being investigated.
He now works at a fast-food restaurant flipping burgers.
"Against my legal advice, he disclosed to his employer that he had been investigated by the ABF," Mr Sutton said.
"They terminated him for lack of transparency and honesty, but how can that be?
"He hadn't even been charged and the reward for his honesty was termination."
Lidden pleaded guilty to offences under Australia's nuclear non-proliferation act that carry a possible 10-year jail sentence.
He is due to receive his sentence from Judge Leonie Flannery on April 11.

data.title: Gemma3 Function Calling
data.author: canyon289
data.article_summary: Gemma 3 发布了新功能，包括128K上下文、图像输入和多语言支持。文章主要介绍了Gemma模型的“函数调用”功能，用户可以通过定义编程接口来完成任务或回答问题。关键点包括：Gemma模型不能自行执行代码，生成的代码需要手动运行或集成到应用中，且在执行前必须验证。Gemma不输出特定于工具的标记，框架需通过检查输出结构来检测工具调用。文章提供了如何构造Gemma提示以使用函数调用的指南，并给出了具体示例，展示了如何定义函数和调用语法。提示结构应遵循特定顺序：函数调用设置和函数定义。文章还强调了指令应简洁明了，以确保模型能正确响应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gemma团队新发布的模型及其功能调用特性，以及对AI模型快速发展的讨论

不同观点：
• canyon289（Gemma团队成员）：介绍Gemma3模型的新特性，特别是在函数调用和提示指令跟随方面的改进。他提到团队发布了相关文档，并引用了伯克利团队的外部验证结果，以证明模型的性能提升。用户可以通过AIstudio或本地自行测试。

• sunrabbit：表达了对AI模型快速发展的惊讶和担忧，尤其是距离GPT首次发布的时间并不长，技术演进速度令人感到震撼。

• minimaxir：讨论了函数调用和结构化输出的技术细节，认为这是展示函数如何在后台运行的清晰示例，但也指出随着代理和MCP的出现，底层工作流程变得更加复杂和混乱。

• zellyn：对是否所有应用都应使用MCP（可能指一种统一的通信协议）提出疑问，暗示不同用例可能需要不同的解决方案。

• mentalgear：赞赏Gemma团队在开源SLM（可能是指语言模型）方面的工作，但提到Google页面在主题设置上存在问题。

• nurettin：认为函数调用只是一种提示方式，目前许多模型都能实现这一功能，暗示Gemma3的这一特性并不独特。

• behnamoh：对Trelis将开源的Llama模型商业化表示不满，认为Gemma新模型的发布打破了Trelis在函数调用能力上的垄断。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是函数调用功能的独特性和新颖性，nurettin认为这一功能并不稀奇，但canyon289和minimaxir则强调了Gemma3在此方面的改进和优势。
• behnamoh对开源模型被商业化的批评，以及对Gemma新模型发布的欢迎，反映了对开源和商业化之间张力的关注。
• 讨论还涉及AI技术发展的快速性及其潜在影响，sunrabbit对此表示担忧。

总的来说，讨论围绕Gemma3新模型的功能、技术细节、市场影响以及AI技术发展的速度展开。

Function calling with Gemma
When using a generative artificial intelligence (AI) model such as Gemma, you
may want to use the model to operate programming interfaces in order to complete
tasks or answer questions. Instructing a model by defining a programming
interface and then making a request that uses that interface is called
function
calling
.
Important:
A Gemma model cannot execute code on its own.
When you
generate code with function calling, you must run the generated code yourself or
run it as part of your application. Always put safeguards in place to validate
any generated code before executing it.
Gemma does not output a tool specific token.
Your framework must detect a tool call by checking if the structure of
the output matches your prompted function output specification.
You can use function calling for a number of applications:
Create a natural language interface
for a programming API to allow
non-programmers to operate a programmatic interface without coding.
Generate programming calls
as part of an AI agent workflow
Function calling is supported in Gemma 3, but the function calling
technique can be used with prior versions of Gemma. This guide provides
instructions on how to construct Gemma prompts that use function calling.
We recommend Gemma3 27B for the best performance,
and Gemma3 12B for balanced performance and latency.
Call programming functions
You can use function calling with Gemma by constructing a prompt that provides
instructions that specify the output format and
define the available functions.
When the user prompt is included, the model outputs a function call,
which is a string that matches your specified output format.
That signals a request to be parsed by your model framework to call the defined
functions.
The following prompting sample
shows a function definition block, along with a function call syntax,
and a function call output from the model.
The following example prompt is meant to be used with a
programming interface for a product catalog:
You have access to functions. If you decide to invoke any of the function(s),
you MUST put it in the format of
[func_name1(params_name1=params_value1, params_name2=params_value2...), func_name2(params)]
You SHOULD NOT include any other text in the response if you call a function
[
{
"name": "get_product_name_by_PID",
"description": "Finds the name of a product by its Product ID",
"parameters": {
"type": "object",
"properties": {
"PID": {
"type": "string"
}
},
"required": [
"PID"
]
}
}
]
While browsing the product catalog, I came across a product that piqued my
interest. The product ID is 807ZPKBL9V. Can you help me find the name of this
product?
This prompt should produce the following response:
[get_product_name_by_PID(PID="807ZPKBL9V")]
This example uses a Python style function call output.
Alternatively, you can specify a JSON style output format, as shown in the
following example:
You have access to functions. If you decide to invoke any of the function(s),
you MUST put it in the format of
{"name": function name, "parameters": dictionary of argument name and its value}
You SHOULD NOT include any other text in the response if you call a function
[
{
"name": "get_product_name_by_PID",
"description": "Finds the name of a product by its Product ID",
"parameters": {
"type": "object",
"properties": {
"PID": {
"type": "string"
}
},
"required": [
"PID"
]
}
}
]
While browsing the product catalog, I came across a product that piqued my
interest. The product ID is 807ZPKBL9V. Can you help me find the name of this
product?
This prompt should produce the following response:
{"name": "get_product_name_by_PID", "parameters": {"PID": "807ZPKBL9V"}}
Components of function calling prompt
When using function calling with Gemma models, your prompt of the model should
follow this specific order and structure:
Function calling
setup
Function
definitions
The following sections provide more detail on each of these prompting
components.
Function calling setup
The
setup
section of the function calling prompt sets the overall expected
behavior of the model. You can add additional, general instructions for the
model's behavior in this section, such as specifying that the output should be
displayed using a
print
or
console.log
function. Use Markdown-style single
backticks (
func_name
) to indicate code syntax.
You have access to functions. If you decide to invoke any of the function(s),
you MUST put it in the format of
{"name": function name, "parameters": dictionary of argument name and its value}
You SHOULD NOT include any other text in the response if you call a function
These instructions should be as clear and brief as possible. Prioritize the
most important instructions and be cautious about providing many general

data.title: High-Performance PNG Decoding
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Blend2D库中新推出的高性能PNG编解码器。PNG格式虽历史悠久，但其编解码性能仍有提升空间，尤其是DEFLATE压缩算法成为性能瓶颈。新编解码器通过优化DEFLATE解码表的构建和快速解码位流，实现了超越其他C、C++等语言编写的编解码器的速度。文章指出，DEFLATE算法由于其标量性质和不适合现代CPU的并行处理特性，性能提升存在上限。优化关键在于快速构建解码表和避免大表带来的性能开销，同时强调针对PNG文件的特定数据集进行调优的重要性。最终，Blend2D的新PNG编解码器在解码速度上取得了显著提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对PNG图像处理优化的必要性和方法

不同观点：
• Pornel认为，针对PNG图像特定数据进行精细优化可以超越通用的inflate实现，并提到了Rust PNG crate的具体例子（lib.rs/fdeflate）来支持这一观点。
• Snickerbockers则表示惊讶，认为优化inflating zlib压缩并不常见，并分享了自己在2016年编写PNG加载器的个人经历。他用的是逐字节处理的方法，尽管硬件性能不高，但仍然能快速加载图像。他认为在毫秒级别的优化上竞争没有太大意义，因为视觉识别图像的时间远大于程序处理时间。他还提到了利用Adam7交错可以提前显示部分图像以“取胜”的可能性。
• Adzm提到了Blend2D项目中使用AsmJit在运行时生成优化的平台特定汇编代码的有趣实践，这与PNG处理优化的讨论相关，但更侧重于动态生成汇编的性能优化技术。

补充讨论：
• Msephton提出了对文章排版的批评，指出移动端样式表没有设置页边距，导致阅读体验不佳。这与技术讨论无直接关系，但强调了用户体验在技术文章阅读中的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 优化的必要性：Pornel和Snickerbockers在优化PNG处理的实际需求上存在分歧。前者关注特定优化的潜在优势，而后者认为通用方法已经足够，特别是在现代硬件上。
• 不同的技术选择：Snickerbockers的逐字节处理方法与Pornel提到的精细优化方法形成对比，展示了不同开发者在处理相同技术问题时的多样化策略。

High-Performance PNG Codec
It's been some time I have written about a
High-Performance QOI Codec
, which joined other codecs offered by Blend2D library in 2024. The development of image codecs continued and now I would like to announce a new high-performance PNG codec, which is much faster than other available codecs written in C, C++, and other programming languages.
Introduction
PNG
is not new; it's been with us for decades and it's most likely one of the most deployed image formats ever, which also means that many others focused on improving the quality of PNG codecs. And indeed, there are many libraries that provide speedy PNG decoding, encoding, or both:
libspng
- written in C, seems faster than the original libpng
wuffs
- written in "WUFFs the language", claims to be
The Fastest, Safest PNG Decoder in the World
zune-png
- written in rust
We can even find pretty interesting statements such as
Memory-safe PNG decoders now vastly outperform C PNG libraries
, etc... However, PNG decoding is fortunately not about a programming language!
DEFLATE - The Challenger
The biggest challenge of decoding PNG images is
DEFLATE
compression algorithm, which is used to compress pixel data, and is the only algorithm allowed by the PNG specification (at least in 2025). DEFLATE aged and is not well suited for modern CPUs that can execute multiple instructions in a single clock cycle in addition to various other features such as out of order execution, branch prediction, etc... In general, everybody who implemented a DEFLATE decoder found a ceiling - at some point it's not possible to improve it further, because it's just inherently scalar and almost impossible to use any kind of SIMD to process the bit-stream.
As a reference, I would like to mention
Iguana
, which clearly shows that in order to utilize SIMD hardware by decoders, the layout of compressed data must be designed for that. And that's something unfixable when it comes to DEFLATE, because that would make it incompatible.
The Way to High Performance Decoding
In general, high-performance decoding of a DEFLATE stream is about the following:
Quickly build decode tables
Quickly decode bit-stream by using these decode tables
Since the maximum DEFLATE code (both litlen and offset) can have at most 15 bits it's not practical to use a single lookup table for all codes, which is why sub-tables are necessary. Conveniently, compression is all about statistics so long codes are much less likely than short codes, which means that a branch misprediction is not really a problem when a sub-table is hit as it won't be hit that often if decode tables are sized well. However, the challenge is to find the optimal size of these tables, because big tables are slower to build, and smaller tables would mean more sub-table lookups. It seems that the sweet spot for high performance DEFLATE decoding is 11 bits for litlen table and 9 bits for offset table (11/9 limit seem to be now widely used across many decoders), but this is just the beginning when optimizing DEFLATE.
Fast Loop
So, what is the most important part of DEFLATE decoder? Is a fast loop! A loop that does bounds checking at the beginning so it doesn't have to do it during decoding of litlen and offset codes. And to perform multiple iterations of fast loop it's better to precalculate the maximum number of possible iterations and just recalculate that again once that number was exhausted. To make the fast loop fast, it's important to optimize for latency, which means using various tricks such as
Reading bits with zero refill latency
.
Big Tables Can Become a Bottleneck
Larger decode tables are fine when there are enough bits to decode, however, if the bit-stream is small, building large decode tables could require much more time than the actual decoding of the bit-stream. The solution is to make the table bits dynamic and to use less bits than maximum when possible. Some bigger PNG files are composed of multiple blocks (even dozens) and each block defines its own Huffman tables, thus, table building should be pretty quick.
The Right Data Corpus
Now I would like to highlight something. Most DEFLATE implementations compare performance against a corpus that doesn't represent compressed PNG data. For example a
Silesia Compression Corpus
is widely used to test implementations of compression and decompression tools, but it doesn't provide data that would match how PNGs are usually compressed. This could mean that tuning a deflate decoder to perform best while decoding Silesia Corpus may not be best for decoding PNG files. The difference between optimal performance can of course vary depending on input images.
For reference, here is a small visual comparison of the structure of a bit-stream that you would see in a Silesia corpus and regular PNG images:
Compressed stream of a file from a Silesia Corpus:
[Beginning of Data]

data.title: A glitch in an online survey replaced the word 'yes' with 'forks'
data.author: cpeterso
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了Pew Research Center在2024年在线调查中遇到的一个技术故障：一些受访者的“yes”选项被错误显示为“forks”。多个受访者反馈了此问题，随后调查团队展开调查。他们发现，故障源于一种“lightbox弹窗”设计特性，导致某些浏览器误以为页面是西班牙语，并自动触发翻译功能。而Google翻译的一个错误将“yes”翻译成了“forks”。此外，问题还导致其他翻译错误，如将“lean”误译为“read”。调查团队确认代码中并无“forks”字样，且之前测试未发现此问题。最终，团队确认该故障不会影响调查数据的可靠性，并解决了问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕翻译工具（如Google Translate）和其他软件中的翻译错误和异常现象的讨论。

不同观点：
• **wat10000**分享了Google Translate在处理"amistad"一词时出现的奇怪错误，特别是在使用不同数量的感叹号时会产生不同的翻译结果，如"friendship!!!"变成"murder!"，揭示了早期翻译工具中存在的奇怪bug。

• **kgeist**描述了一个客户在平台上遇到的文档损坏问题，其中莫名其妙地出现了足球明星的名字（如"Messi"和"Zidane"）。这被归因于一个损坏的浏览器扩展，类似于Google Translate的错误，表明翻译工具可能在特定情况下引发不可预见的问题。

• **miki123211**指出了在软件翻译中常见的歧义问题，特别是单一词汇在不同上下文中的多种翻译方式，例如"branch"可以指分支机构或树的分支，"book"可以指预订或书籍。这些错误对屏幕阅读器用户更为明显，因为它们隐藏在可访问性标签中。

• **once_inc**分享了一个由于Excel翻译荷兰姓氏而引发的趣事，其中"van"被翻译成"Busje"，导致客户名称出错，但在被市场部门发现后引发了笑声。

• **Dylan16807**表达了对技术句子理解的困惑，特别是涉及网页文本翻译和自动弹出窗口的修复，显示了对技术细节的不确定性。

• **frnx**质疑Google Translate近年来质量下降的原因，指出其在简单翻译中出现疯狂循环和重复句子的现象，质疑是否有足够的质量检查。

• **ineedasername**提到在使用[forks]和[spoons]作为代理变量时的策略性操作，揭示了在数据分析和结果操控中的潜在问题。

• **withinrafael**分享了Windows在英式英语用户菜单中出现的奇怪翻译"Compress to postcode"。

• **epistasis**对复杂bug和实际结果表示赞赏，表现出对技术异常的积极接受。

• **rkunde**指出Chrome在遇到"403 Forbidden"页面时会错误地提示“翻译自丹麦语”。

• **yuliyp**提到在一次知识竞赛中，由于浏览器自动翻译导致问题变得更容易，影响了比赛的公平性。

• **perching_aix**提到OpenAI的ChatGPT界面使用机器翻译，也出现了类似的错误，但没有明确的报告途径。

• **banqjls**和**FabHK**澄清了"forks"并不对应于西班牙语中的"yes"，并对Google Translate近期的更新问题表示不满。

补充讨论：
• 翻译工具在处理单一词汇和特定符号时由于缺乏上下文而导致的错误。
• 翻译错误在不同软件和平台中的普遍性及其引发的实际问题和趣事。
• 对翻译工具质量和更新过程的质疑，特别是在错误明显增加的情况下。
• 翻译错误对不同用户群体（如屏幕阅读器用户）的潜在影响。
